# Vendored dependency patches

`netdev` 0.46.3 (MIT, upstream https://github.com/shellrow/netdev) is pinned by netwatch. Its Darwin IPv6 flags implementation refers to `libc::in6_ifreq`, which libc exposes only on macOS. The local patch retains the upstream macOS behavior and returns unavailable/default per-address flags on iOS, as netdev does for unsupported platforms. Address enumeration still uses getifaddrs. Remove the patch when upstream supports iOS without this macOS-only type. All other source files are unchanged.

`netwatch` 0.19.3 (MIT/Apache-2.0, upstream https://github.com/n0-computer/net-tools) routes iOS through macOS-only libc routing structures. The patch gives iOS address enumeration through netdev/getifaddrs and a five-second cancellable foreground monitor. Default-route and home-router metadata remain unavailable. App suspension destroys the endpoint/monitor and resume re-enumerates addresses. The UDP wrapper uses noq-udp's `try_send` API on all platforms, preserving readiness retries and socket rebind handling while returning send errors to callers. An oversized-datagram regression test covers all five noq send paths. The manifest also uses the current `unused_async` Clippy lint spelling.

Run the UDP tests with `cargo test --manifest-path vendor/netwatch/Cargo.toml --target-dir crates/target --lib udp::tests`.

`swarm-discovery` 0.6.5 (Apache-2.0, upstream https://github.com/rkuhn/swarm-discovery) needs three DNS-SD compatibility fixes for Bonjour: enable hickory-proto's `mdns` feature to decode the cache-flush class bit, include an empty TXT record when there is no metadata, and match SRV/TXT/A/AAAA across answer and additional sections. The service type, peer IDs, ports, address grouping, nonempty TXT attributes, socket implementation, and liveness algorithm are unchanged. The source was copied from the registry archive with SHA-256 `d7e56b7e93eaffb9baba3e64936a5912540847516fc5f26d66ad18044b8d4a14`; production differences are limited to `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.toml.orig`, `src/sender.rs`, and `src/receiver.rs`. The two Rust modules also contain packet-level regression tests. Remove the patch after upstream includes these fixes. Like the other workspace patches, this applies to builds from this checkout; independently published crates need the equivalent upstream dependency fixes.

Run its library tests with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$PWD/crates/target" cargo test --manifest-path vendor/swarm-discovery/Cargo.toml --lib`. Native CI runs these on Linux and macOS. The optional same-LAN test `python3 apps/mobile/tool/bonjour_probe.py --ssh-host macbook` checks an ephemeral offline iroh endpoint against the Mac's OS `dns-sd` browse, resolve, SRV query, GetAddrInfo, and registration. It uses no stored identities or enrollment and checks resolution only. It does not validate QUIC, iOS permissions, IPv6 link-local scope IDs, cross-packet record aggregation, or changes across network/lifecycle transitions.
